claims.text: A 12-year-old boy with severe rheumatic heart disease had mitral, tricuspid and aortic valve repair at age 9, then haemolytic anaemia, jaundice and mitral regurgitation, and mitral valve replacement with a 25 mm On-X valve, anticoagulated with warfarin. Three months before presentation his prosthetic valve function was normal. Weighing 75 kg (BMI 31), he presented to a regional Emergency Department with acute pulmonary oedema after diving into water from about 2 m.

Transthoracic echocardiography on admission gave a mean mitral inflow gradient of 20 mmHg without obvious regurgitation but limited valve assessment. He deteriorated, was intubated and ventilated with inotropes, and transoesophageal echocardiography showed an absent mechanical valve leaflet with severe mitral regurgitation.
